highlights.title: Split production runtime
highlights.description: Web, Scheduler, General Worker, Critical Worker, Bulk Worker, and Status Projector can scale independently. The integrated runtime remains supported.

highlights.title: Notification delivery control plane
highlights.description: Durable logical intents, provider attempts, traffic classes, admission/defer behavior, retry and terminal states, callback reconciliation, provider capacity controls, and an administrator Operations view. Delivery evidence distinguishes deferred, retrying, accepted, delivered, permanent-failure, and superseded work.

highlights.title: Microsoft Teams ChatOps
highlights.description: Entra application and Azure Bot integration, Teams app packaging and tenant installation, service-to-channel destinations, Adaptive Cards, interactive incident actions, identity linking, war rooms, participant synchronization, and meeting collaboration. A service can target up to three Teams destinations.

highlights.title: Twilio voice paging
highlights.description: `VOICE` is a triggered-incident paging channel with responder acknowledgement input, signed callbacks, and reconciliation of uncertain provider outcomes. Acknowledge and resolve lifecycle updates do not initiate additional voice calls.

highlights.title: Incident response policy engine
highlights.description: Versioned classification, incident SLA, and support-hours policies at workspace and service scope, with immutable published versions, preview, history, diff, restore, and API access.

highlights.title: SCIM 2.0 provisioning
highlights.description: Users, Groups, discovery endpoints, provisioning/deprovisioning, team membership, PATCH operations, and in-product bearer-token generation, rotation, and revocation.

highlights.title: Auditor access and sessions
highlights.description: A read-oriented `AUDITOR` role, centralized resource authorization, OIDC claim mapping, and a canonical signed-in-session registry with browser, OS, device, authentication type, activity, expiry, and revoke controls.

highlights.title: Privacy and compliance operations
highlights.description: Privacy/DSAR request processing, export and erasure evidence, retention holds, controlled encryption migrations, technical control evaluation, framework mappings, evidence ledgers, drift monitoring, and verifiable evidence-package exports. Framework mapping does not confer external certification.

highlights.title: Docker Swarm
highlights.description: Integrated and split stacks, Raft secrets, direct-database migration lifecycle, health checks, topology switching, and rollback tooling.

highlights.title: Deployment planning and load certification
highlights.description: Workload shapes and multi-topology load/correctness tests cover ingestion, incident lifecycle, escalation, notification fanout, realtime delivery, status fanout, and recovery.

highlights.title: ManageEngine ingestion
highlights.description: A new native inbound parser joins the existing integration catalog. The release certifies 28 current inbound contracts in total; it does not add 28 new integrations.

highlights.title: Incident response
highlights.description: Centralized lifecycle commands, durable side effects, persistent idempotency, stale-worker fencing, a global create modal, templates, stronger validation, rebuilt incident detail, action items, and interactive 5-Whys postmortems.

highlights.title: Schedules and escalation
highlights.description: Redesigned schedule setup/detail, DST-safe rotations, overrides and handoff behavior, user/team/schedule escalation targets, priority/urgency/support-hours conditions, durable recovery, and stale-work protection.

highlights.title: Slack and Jira
highlights.description: More reliable Slack war rooms, identity and capability controls, up to three Slack destinations per service, provider-neutral collaboration, and stronger bidirectional Jira lifecycle reconciliation.

highlights.title: Quiet Hours
highlights.description: Personal timezone-aware suppression for low-urgency notifications; medium- and high-urgency operational paging bypasses Quiet Hours.

highlights.title: Status Page V3
highlights.description: One supported status page with themes, announcements, subscriber verification/unsubscribe, API tokens, webhooks, privacy controls, uptime history/export, rebuild-safe snapshots, and hardened routing. Multiple status pages are not a supported 2.0 capability.

highlights.title: Dashboards and reports
highlights.description: Templates, configurable widgets, persisted layout, private/team/organization visibility, filtered share links, PDF export, live refresh, and fullscreen NOC/TV presentation mode.

highlights.title: Responder-grade mobile PWA
highlights.description: Rebuilt mobile navigation and operational workflows, per-device push registration and reconciliation, repair flows, offline/cached-state boundaries, update handling, and hardened fresh-install iOS Web Push recovery. This is an installable PWA, not a native App Store application.

highlights.title: OIDC and SSO policy
highlights.description: Entra, Google, Okta, Auth0, and generic provider flows with PKCE/nonce, JIT provisioning, explicit account linking, claim-to-role mapping, provider lifecycle hardening, maximum lifetime, update interval, idle timeout, and reauthentication controls.

highlights.title: Application bootstrap and routing
highlights.description: Short-lived first-admin bootstrap capability, UI-managed Application URL, canonical-host enforcement, reverse-proxy awareness, and explicit HTTP 421 protection.

highlights.title: Health and operations
highlights.description: Expanded Health Center diagnostics, Prometheus metrics, system logs, backup/restore, worker/readiness visibility, and PgBouncer-aware connection ownership.

highlights.title: Documentation
highlights.description: The 2.0 task-oriented documentation is backed by implementation discovery, semantic contracts, runtime evidence, API smoke tests, legacy-knowledge mapping, and rendered-site validation.

highlights.title: License
highlights.description: OpsKnight 2.0.0 is the first stable release distributed under `AGPL-3.0-only`. OpsKnight 1.4.0 and earlier retain their historical licenses.

products.label: Incident command
products.headline: One place to run the incident.
products.description: Keep ownership, responders, timeline, notes and action items together from first alert to resolution.
features: Keep a timeline and action items

story.title: One incident, with the context to act.
story.body: An incoming signal belongs to a service. Priority, urgency, ownership and related alert context give the responder a place to begin instead of another isolated notification.

story.title: Acknowledge. Assign. Investigate.
story.body: Acknowledge the incident, assign a responder and record the investigation. Keep notes, watchers and the operational timeline together so the next person can understand the response.

story.title: Response timing with a policy behind it.
story.body: Use the documented response-policy and SLA workflow to inspect acknowledgement and resolution timing. Review the applicable policy and support-hours context before interpreting a breach.

story.title: Coordinate without losing the record.
story.body: Create a provider-backed war room when collaboration is needed. OpsKnight remains authoritative for incident state while Slack or Teams projects the response into the conversation.

story.title: Recovery is the beginning of learning.
story.body: Resolve the incident, preserve the response timeline and carry follow-up work into a postmortem with accountable owners.

products.label: On-call & escalation
products.headline: Know who’s responsible before something breaks.
products.description: Build rotations, schedule overrides and escalation policies around the people responsible for each service.
features: User, team and schedule escalation targets

story.title: A schedule is a promise of ownership.
story.body: Build rotations around real team availability, time zones and coverage. Verify the effective on-call responder instead of relying on how a calendar looks.

story.title: Change coverage without rebuilding the rotation.
story.body: Use an override for planned leave or a last-minute swap. Review its time window and validate that the intended responder owns the affected interval.

story.title: Primary, backup, and a viable final target.
story.body: An escalation step can target a user, team or effective schedule. Set explicit delays and channels, then test unavailable users and empty schedules before relying on the policy.

story.title: Make the handoff deliberate.
story.body: Review active incidents, current ownership and incoming coverage together. A schedule transition is an operational handoff, not a guarantee that every open incident was understood.

story.title: Test the page before you need it.
story.body: Validate the selected responder, healthy endpoints and delivery evidence with a synthetic incident. A saved schedule alone does not prove an end-to-end page.

products.label: Paging
products.headline: Reach the responder. Not just their inbox.
products.description: Route urgent pages through configured providers and inspect attempts, retries and terminal delivery outcomes.

story.title: Intent first. Delivery evidence next.
story.body: The notification control plane stores a logical intent and provider-specific attempts. Routing and admission decide eligible work; callbacks add delivery evidence without rewriting the incident lifecycle.

story.title: Critical, transactional and bulk work.
story.body: Notification priority and worker lanes keep time-sensitive response work distinguishable from general and bulk processing. Inspect admission, oldest queue age and lane health together when capacity is constrained.

story.title: Route to people and service destinations.
story.body: Configure lifecycle events, channels and healthy responder endpoints. Slack and Teams service destinations receive lifecycle messages; linked destinations are not an ordered fallback chain.

story.title: Voice for the triggered incident.
story.body: Twilio voice paging supports responder acknowledgement input. Acknowledgement and resolution events do not start additional voice calls. Test the call input against the actual incident state.

story.title: Retry the operation, not the incident.
story.body: Transient failures, provider rate limits, deferred work and permanent failures require different actions. Inspect the existing retry schedule, respect provider hints and correct bad credentials or endpoints before retrying.

story.title: Accepted is not the same as delivered.
story.body: Trace the notification ID, attempts, provider message ID, callback outcome and next-attempt time. Superseded intents are discarded when a newer incident state makes them stale.

story.title: See the failure where it happened.
story.body: Use Notifications Operations and Health Center to connect provider failures, capacity and worker availability. Provider delivery is an operational outcome to verify, not a promise attached to a queued page.

products.label: ChatOps
products.headline: Response belongs in the room.
products.description: Coordinate incidents in Slack and Microsoft Teams with incident actions, linked identities and war rooms.
features: Service destinations for Slack and Teams

story.title: Choose the conversation that owns the response.
story.body: Create an incident-scoped Slack or Microsoft Teams war room manually, or use the effective global/service policy for automatic creation. One destination should own automatic room creation for a service.

story.title: Keep actions attached to the incident.
story.body: Provider cards project incident context and supported actions. Identity links, product permissions, provider capabilities and lifecycle phase determine which actions can run.

story.title: Policy before provisioning.
story.body: Service policy overrides the global default. Validate the effective destination and permissions with a new incident; changing policy does not migrate an already provisioned room.

story.title: Reconcile drift instead of creating duplicates.
story.body: Inspect the durable room and operation identity when provisioning times out, membership changes or a card is stale. Retry or reconcile the existing operation before attempting another room.

story.title: Close the response with the conversation.
story.body: Resolve the incident, verify terminal context and close or archive the room through supported controls. Provider retention and cleanup capabilities determine the final room behavior.

products.label: Status page
products.headline: Give customers clarity.
products.description: Publish service status, incident updates and maintenance without exposing your internal response timeline.

story.title: Internal response. Deliberate public communication.
story.body: Map services to customer-facing components and choose approved impact wording. Projection controls the fields that cross the privacy boundary; it does not serialize the internal incident directly.

story.title: Publish, verify, correct, resolve.
story.body: Confirm affected components, publish a scoped update and open the page through the audience’s hostname while signed out. Follow with a correcting update or resolution and verify the public state again.

story.title: A page and its subscribers are separate outcomes.
story.body: Subscriber and webhook delivery are asynchronous and separate from page rendering. Review verification, unsubscribe and API-access behavior, then inspect delivery independently.

story.title: Brand the customer-facing surface.
story.body: Configure the installation’s supported status page, service mapping and privacy options. Verify DNS, TLS and the public URL when using a custom domain.

story.title: History with an operational boundary.
story.body: Service availability and incident history give customers context. Check projection freshness, privacy settings and documented metrics before treating the public view as current.

products.label: Analytics
products.headline: See the shape of your operations.
products.description: Use incident and service performance data to understand response times, trends and SLA outcomes.

story.title: Measure the response, not just the alert count.
story.body: Explore incident volume, acknowledgement and resolution timing with the available dashboard filters. Compare like-for-like time windows and service context.

story.title: Keep current state and historical timing distinct.
story.body: An active incident count describes the current response. MTTA and MTTR describe timing across the selected population; inspect the sample and filters before drawing conclusions.

story.title: Bring the questions back to the team.
story.body: Use the analysis to identify repeated incidents and response bottlenecks, then connect findings to owned postmortem action items. Metrics support investigation rather than explaining root cause on their own.

story.title: Verify the evidence behind a review.
story.body: Record the selected time range and service scope when sharing a finding. Follow the analytics guide to understand available views and operational limitations.

products.label: Postmortems
products.headline: Make the next incident easier.
products.description: Turn resolved incidents into reviews with a timeline, contributing factors and owned follow-up work.
features: Action items with owners and due dates

story.title: Start from the incident evidence.
story.body: Connect impact, detection, response and resolution to the source timeline. Preserve evidence links so the review remains traceable to the incident record.

story.title: Draft. Review. Publish.
story.body: Separate investigation from the published review. Distinguish observed facts from hypotheses and write for system improvement rather than individual blame.

story.title: Learning needs an owner.
story.body: Track follow-up action items with an owner and status. Close remediation work when it is verifiably complete, rather than when the incident review is written.

story.title: Carry the change into the next response.
story.body: Review detection gaps, response friction and contributing conditions together. Use the documented workflow to keep review and publication deliberate.

products.label: Mobile
products.headline: Your response travels with you.
products.description: Install the progressive web app and acknowledge, triage and follow incidents from your phone.

story.title: The response fits in your pocket.
story.body: Use the mobile incident routes with the same installation identity and permissions. Keep active incidents and their context accessible away from the desktop.

story.title: Install the progressive web app.
story.body: Follow the device and browser-specific installation guide. Mobile is a PWA, not a separate app-store product.

story.title: Register each device deliberately.
story.body: Enable Web Push, grant the required browser permission and validate the device endpoint with the notification workflow. Delivery behavior depends on the browser and device.

story.title: Verify before relying on it.
story.body: Test notifications and incident access on the actual phone. Device permission, endpoint registration and product authorization are separate checks.

products.label: Security & identity
products.headline: Your infrastructure. Your users. Your keys.
products.description: Connect identity, control access and inspect operational evidence on infrastructure you own.

story.title: Identity belongs to your organization.
story.body: Connect OIDC authentication and provision users and groups with SCIM. Enforce MFA at your identity provider; OpsKnight does not provide a native server-verified second factor.

story.title: Access is an operational control.
story.body: Review roles, scoped authorization and session behavior. Provisioning and deprovisioning should be verified against the effective product permissions.

story.title: Keys and infrastructure have an owner.
story.body: Configure secrets, network access, HTTPS and recovery for your deployment. Preserve required encryption keys separately from database backups and follow the key-rotation guide.

story.title: Prepare evidence for your evaluation.
story.body: Use the security and procurement entry point for release policies, vulnerability handling, SBOM scope, supported versions and shared responsibility. These materials do not confer external certification.

products.label: Operations
products.headline: The platform has to survive the incident too.
products.description: Choose integrated or split runtimes and inspect worker health, delivery operations, metrics and logs.

story.title: Scale the responsibility that is constrained.
story.body: Choose an integrated process or separate Web, Scheduler, General Worker, Critical Worker, Bulk Worker and Status Projector. A split runtime alone does not provide high availability.

story.title: Workers, queues and providers tell different stories.
story.body: Inspect worker heartbeat, oldest pending job age and provider state together. A growing critical queue has a different operational priority from delayed bulk work.

story.title: Budget database connections before adding replicas.
story.body: Include each role’s replica count and pool size in the connection budget. More workers can exhaust database capacity instead of improving queue latency.

story.title: Use PgBouncer where the topology calls for it.
story.body: Follow the documented transaction-pooling and direct-connection requirements. Schema management and runtime traffic must use the connection paths appropriate to their work.

story.title: Health Center for investigation. Metrics for monitoring.
story.body: Use the Health Center to inspect recorded diagnostics and operational priorities. Connect documented health and Prometheus metrics to your own monitoring, and interpret component status rather than only HTTP status.

story.title: Make scale and recovery a tested plan.
story.body: Scale the constrained role only after checking database and provider capacity. Plan backups, upgrades, ingress and recovery together for production availability.

notifications.voiceScope: Triggered incidents with responder acknowledgement input. Acknowledgement and resolution events do not initiate additional calls.

models.title: Docker Compose
models.description: Start with the integrated runtime and PostgreSQL. Split the runtime when independent scaling is useful.

models.title: Kubernetes
models.description: Use Kubernetes manifests, Helm or Kustomize with integrated and split runtime profiles.

models.title: Docker Swarm
models.description: Run integrated or split stacks with Swarm secrets and documented upgrade workflows.

sections.title: Identity
sections.description: Authenticate with OIDC and provision users and groups through SCIM 2.0.

sections.title: Provisioning
sections.description: Manage user and group lifecycle through SCIM discovery, tokens and provisioning endpoints.

sections.title: Access & sessions
sections.description: Use roles, scoped authorization and the signed-in-session registry.

sections.title: Privacy operations
sections.description: Process privacy requests and retention holds with operational evidence.

sections.title: Deployment hardening
sections.description: Configure secrets, networking and operational access for your environment.

boundaries.manualEscalation: Capability-enabled Microsoft Teams cards; no manual escalation control in Web or standard Slack incident actions.
